Short title: Historical flood geography and physical context in Johor Bahru.
Frozen caption: (A) Frozen F01–F19 historical flood evidence-support zones across the Johor Bahru District. (B) Urban-core detail showing the spatial concentration of road- and community-based flood zones. (C) The same frozen zones over the independent strict low-lying terrain screen. Red, yellow and blue polygons denote Severe, Recurrent and Mild historical classes, respectively. The polygons represent evidence-support areas and are not interpreted as complete hydraulic inundation extents.

Short title: Spatial integration of flood evidence, road disruption and healthcare accessibility.
Frozen caption: (A) Frozen historical flood zones, major roads, acute/emergency hospitals and observed 2025 road-disruption sections. (B) Subdistrict-level newly unreachable rates and the population origins that became unreachable in the primary 20 March 2025 event. (C) Recovery stage of the initially isolated origins under the nominal J105 → FT01 → FT003 restoration sequence.

Short title: Observed road-disruption correspondence across historical and quantitative events.
Frozen caption: (A) 2023 same-road operational consequences for the frozen road-type flood zones, including the explicit Jalan Kolam Ayer closure and the source-limited Gertak Merah corridor. (B) Spatially authorized 2025 JKR disruption sections relative to the frozen historical zones. The 2025 disruptions extend beyond the localized recurrent-zone footprint, showing that F01–F19 should not be treated as an exhaustive hazard map.

Short title: Healthcare-accessibility impact and spatial concentration of the 20 March 2025 road disruption.
Frozen caption: (A) Corrected baseline and event-level unreachable population. (B) Single-road attribution of newly unreachable population. (C) Subdistrict concentration of newly unreachable population. The principal event effect is loss of network reachability rather than a large citywide increase in mean travel time among origins that remain reachable.

Short title: Robustness of accessibility loss and road-recovery priorities.
Frozen caption: (A) Newly unreachable population across 27 declared closure-location combinations. (B) Criticality-rank robustness of the four observed road disruptions. (C) Population-access recovery achieved after the first and second restoration steps across all six recovery sequences. J105 has the highest nominal effect but is location-sensitive, while FT01 remains a stable Tier-1 corridor.
